# Pivot Budget Controller

## Mandate
Hope is not a strategy; neither is the fifth rename of the same variable. Rank 1–2 forbid infinite surface retries; this policy adds **counting rules** so you pivot mechanism early enough to matter.

## Track failure classes
Bucket repeated failures by **stable signature**, not by emotional similarity:
- Same assertion text / same error code family / same stage (compile vs runtime vs wrong answer).

## Budget (default)
- **Two strikes, same class**: the third attempt **must** change mechanism—different architecture (e.g. library vs hand-rolled), different IO path, rewrite vs patch, isolate minimal repro, or swap data source **within** what the brief allows.
- **Third strike** in that class still present after mechanism change: stop tweaking; escalate to the smallest out-of-repo repro or wholesale file rewrite when cheaper than archaeology.

## Attempt log (lightweight)
One line per try: `change → new outcome prefix`. If you cannot describe the change, you are not ready to edit.

## Pair with verification
Every pivot begins by re-confirming **ground facts** with the real verifier and read-back—pivots on bad measurements just spin.

## Anti-patterns
- Cosmetic edits that preserve the same failing branch behavior.
- Rising retry count without naming the failure class in writing (even brief internal notes).

## Why this beats 1–4 alone
Turns “don’t loop” into an **operational circuit breaker** that fires before sunk-cost lock-in.
